cards.details: Birth of Vardhamana Mahavira at Kundagrama near Vaishali.
Renunciation: Left his home at the age of 30 to lead an ascetic life.
Attained Kevala Jnana (Omniscience) at Jrimbhikagrama under a Sal tree.
Mahaparinirvana at Pava (near Rajagriha) at the age of 72.

items.title: J.I.N.A
items.decryption: Jina means Conqueror (of senses), Indriya refers to senses, Nirgrantha means bond-free, Ahinsa is the core doctrine.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Commonly confused: Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara, NOT the founder of Jainism; he systematized earlier teachings.
Chronology trap: Mahavira was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha and Bimbisara, not Ashoka.
Location error: Mahavira attained Kevala Jnana at Jrimbhikagrama, not under a Bodhi tree (that is Buddha).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Birth: Kundagrama (Vaishali)
  • Enlightenment: Jrimbhikagrama (Bank of Rijupalika river)
  • Death: Pava (near Rajagriha)

Family

  • Father: Siddhartha (Jnatrika clan)
  • Mother: Trishala (Lichchhavi princess)
  • Wife: Yashoda
  • Daughter: Anojja/Priyadarshana

Mindmap: Life of Mahavira

  • Early Life: Kshatriya prince of the Jnatrika clan
  • Great Renunciation: Left worldly life at 30
  • Spiritual Journey: Twelve years of intense penance
  • Attainment: Kevalin (the omniscient)
    • First sermon at Vipulachala hill, Rajagriha
    • Sangha formed with 11 disciples (Ganadharas)
FeatureJain Philosophy
Core DoctrineAnekantavada (Many-sidedness)
Ethical CodeAnuvratas and Mahavratas
SalvationTri-ratna (Right Faith, Knowledge, Conduct)
